bull_bear.body: Debt-free balance sheet; reinvestment into capacity expansion (5 new plants in last 12 months); focus on working capital to maintain high inventory levels (68% imported PVC) ensuring supply continuity.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Jal Jeevan/Nal Se Jal fund release delays (state-center coordination issues); PVC price volatility causing channel destocking; Geopolitical tensions impacting exports and feedstock; Unseasonal rainfall affecting agri demand.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; emphasizes volume growth over value due to price volatility; transparent about government spending delays; confident in market share gains despite industry contraction.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Industry volume contracted 9% in FY26 while Supreme grew 14%, implying massive market share shift from unorganized/smaller players; China's coal-based PVC production insulates domestic prices from Gulf crude volatility; Windows business margins expected to be superior to core piping due to customization.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Company is Debt Free and having Cash Surplus of Rs. 542 Crores as at 30th June'26" under Strong Liquidity.
- USP list states "Strong Cash Flows to fund expansion plans".
- Stated aim of "Optimisation of shareholder value" via "Higher ROACE" and "Liberal dividend payout".
- Carries an AA+ CRISIL Stable Rating; market cap stated as 40000+ Cr as at 30th June'26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Piping: +14% vol, +11% value (CPVC +38% vol); Industrial: -1% vol, -3% value; Packaging: +5% vol, +3% value; Consumer: +4% vol, -1% value. Value-added products grew 15% to INR 4,677 Cr.

business.body:

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as "Powered by a robust infrastructure and expertise, Supreme is India's largest plastic manufacturing and processing company", founded in 1942 with "80+ years in the industry".
- Stated USPs include "Diversified product portfolio with established Brand Equity", "Significant Market Share in each of the verticals" and "Pan India Distribution Network and Reach".
- Claims to be "Invulnerable from import substitutes" and a "User of diverse plastics materials".
- At-a-glance moat markers: 55 export countries, 7000+ distributors, 6500+ employee strength and an AA+ CRISIL Stable rating.
- Brand/trade ecosystem described as "An integrated ecosystem driving brand leadership, digital customer connect, and technical plumber training across India", with 5 Knowledge Centers, 100% Pan-India Reach, 4+ social platforms and 2 dedicated apps (Pipe and Furniture divisions).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group] The Supreme Group comprises The Supreme Industries Ltd, Supreme Petrochem Ltd and Supreme Industries Overseas (FZE), a wholly owned UAE subsidiary — deck-level group figures should not be read as the listed entity alone.
- [Leadership] M. P. Taparia is Chairman & Managing Director; P C Somani is CFO; the management team is listed by vertical (e.g. A K Tripathi, Exe. VP Plastic Piping System; V L Malu, Exe. VP Industrial Components; Vivek Taparia, President Packaging).
- [Trade engagement] 5 regional Knowledge Centers impart technical education on plumbing best fitting practices and solvent welding, alongside plumber workshops and global trade fair participation.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 margins supported by INR 70-80 Cr Q4 inventory gain; FY27 guidance 14-14.5% assumes normalized raw material costs. Current PVC prices dropped INR 34/kg in April, creating potential inventory loss headwinds for Q1 FY27. Labor code provisioning finalized at INR 14.4 Cr.

outlook.body: FY27 Volume Growth: 12-13% overall, 15-17% for Piping segment; EBITDA Margin: 14.0-14.5%; Order Inflow: Agri demand picked up in April post-price correction; Capex: INR 1,000 Cr committed for FY27.

outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Windows & Doors unit (Kanpur) started March '26, targeting INR 250 Cr annual revenue at full capacity with higher margins; Gas piping (electro-fusion fittings) expansion; Export target scaling from $5 Mn to $50 Mn; New packaging facility planned near JNPT.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Supreme Industries delivered 12% volume growth in FY26 despite a 9% industry contraction, driven by market share gains and a ~INR 70-80 Cr Q4 inventory gain from PVC price spikes. Guidance for FY27 targets 12-13% overall volume growth (15-17% in piping) with margins stabilizing at 14-14.5%, though immediate Q1 faces margin pressure from falling resin prices.

open.item: Southern unit for popular, high-demand pallet models is set to begin production in the first quarter of the current year (the Eastern unit has already commenced production).

Company plans to launch the 'Cross Plastics' product in Q2 of the current year, subject to further refinements and successful trials (trials already conducted at customer sites; feedback under evaluation).
Company expects double-digit volume growth in the current year, supported by several initiatives already taken.
HPCL, another oil marketing company, is expected to float a tender for LPG cylinders during the current year, and the Company expects to participate with a positive outcome.
Company has scaled up solar capacity to 43.30 MWp as of FY26 and has set a target to further increase solar capacity to 10 MWp by FY27 (as stated in the report).

Company is planning to commission four new manufacturing units during the current year: Near Patna (Bihar) — Pipe Systems; Kathua near Jammu (J&K) — Pipe Systems; Gadegaon near Jalgaon (Maharashtra) — Solvents and Adhesives; Malanpur (M.P.) — Material Handling Systems, with investment in excess of ₹1000 crores this year.
Company is targeting 140 million kWh of renewable energy usage by FY 2026-27, up from 125.84 million kWh consumed in FY 2025-26.
Double Materiality Assessment is in progress during the year; the detailed report will be published in the next sustainability report for FY26-27.
Company expects to sell the full capacity of the new Kanpur Dehat Windows & Doors facility by next year, which will enable it to expand capacity at the same site.

Two new greenfield plants for the Plastic Piping Division at Jammu & Bihar (land already in Company's possession) are to be taken up for execution in the current financial year and are likely to go into production during FY26-27.

Company plans further capacity/technology initiatives at PPD plants: relocating and upgrading an EPE line from Urse to Jadcherla; technical overhauling of EPE machines and installing a new Calendar Roll at Hosur; overhauling a Toshiba machine and installing a Calendar Roll at Malanpur; and an XLPE line under evaluation at Kharagpur.
Company has contracted capital-account commitments of ₹323.31 crores remaining to be executed (net of advances) as at 31 March 2026.

Protective Packaging Division is pursuing ongoing capacity expansion and technology upgradation initiatives across Malanpur, Jadcherla, Hosur, Kharagpur and Urse plants (new/relocated lines, machine overhauls, Calendar Roll installations).
Performance Films Division's expansion strategy focuses on increasing footprint across Middle East, EU, South America, Africa, and Southeast Asia.

BPCL's initial order for 2,00,000 nos. 10 Kg LPG Cylinders has been successfully executed, with a repeat order for similar quantity under execution; IOCL's LOI for 2,31,035 nos. remains under execution at a slower pace.
Company has invested in a recognised start-up venture to carry out developmental activities for composite pressure vessels and light-weighting of existing products.

Protective Packaging Division has completed land acquisition for a proposed greenfield manufacturing facility in the Western region near a port, evaluating product lines (PU Sheets, PU Moulding, XLPE, NBR, IXPE, Capcell, Litecell, PP Moulding) to serve export and West-zone customers.

Prices of Polymers other than PVC remain at elevated levels due to production stoppages in Gulf polymer units and crude-oil movement restrictions from the West Asia conflict; management expects these to ease gradually after the war ends.
Company has engaged additional human resources to avail the emerging export opportunity from India's FTAs, aiming to boost exports of Company products.
Company has committed to a 1.5°C Net Zero Science Based Target under SBTi.

risks.note: Shifts in US tariff policies may disrupt global trade flows and impact export competitiveness; mitigated by a diversified procurement strategy (including sourcing from China) and the fact that about 98% of Company sales are domestic.

Persistent conflicts and regional tensions affect supply chains and energy costs; mitigated through a multi-vendor sourcing strategy for raw materials and maintaining strategic safety stocks of critical raw materials.
risks.risk: Geopolitical instability affecting supply chains and energy costs

risks.note: Slower growth in major economies may lead to reduced infrastructure spending; the Company focuses on domestic high-growth sectors such as urban infrastructure, agriculture and water management (including participation in various Government initiatives) to offset global headwinds.
risks.risk: Global economic slowdown reducing infrastructure spending

risks.note: As an importer of key raw materials, currency volatility impacts margins; managed through a consistent hedging policy using forward contracts and natural hedging (to some extent). Being debt-free, the Company has no currency/interest-rate risk from long-term or short-term foreign currency loans.

Delays in large-scale capex projects can lead to cost overruns; mitigated via cost-benefit analysis and stipulated timelines before beginning any capex project, with periodic progress tracking against budget by the Project Management team.

Cybersecurity, technology and operational risks are integral to the Company's enterprise risk management framework; mitigated through layered network security controls, AI-enabled threat detection, periodic vulnerability assessments, security audits and control reviews, plus business continuity and disaster recovery frameworks.
Risk of product failure is mitigated by subjecting every batch to stringent pressure and stress testing according to international standards (BIS/ISO).
The Company rigorously defends its trademarks, designs and patents, with its legal team proactively monitoring the market for infringements to protect market share and premium brand positioning.
